Personnel Records – Meridian Biosample Core

Annual Performance Review Summaries, Review Period: 1 Jan 2024 – 31 Dec 2024

Note: The following summaries were compiled from the individual review meetings held in the last two weeks of December 2024. All staff were rated on a 1–5 scale (1 = Does Not Meet Expectations, 2 = Needs Improvement, 3 = Meets Expectations, 4 = Exceeds Expectations, 5 = Outstanding). Each summary includes the employee’s self-assessment highlights, supervisor comments, overall rating, areas for improvement, and development plan for 2025. Signed copies are filed in the HR cabinet (drawer 3).

---

1. Dr. Nurul Huda – Senior Research Scientist

Self-Assessment: Dr. Nurul noted that she had led the validation of the new cryopreservation protocol for PBMC samples, which was successfully adopted in Q2. She also highlighted her supervision of two junior staff and her role in troubleshooting the liquid nitrogen alarm system after the August incident. She rated her own performance as 4, citing that her administrative workload had increased more than expected and that this had limited her bench time.

Supervisor Comments: Dr. Nurul has been a reliable and technically strong member of the core. Her work on the cryopreservation protocol was thorough and well-documented. She has also been proactive in mentoring Wei Lin and Farah. However, her documentation of the alarm system troubleshooting was delayed by about two weeks, which caused some confusion during the audit preparation. Overall, her technical output remains high.

Overall Rating: 4 (Exceeds Expectations)

Areas for Improvement: (1) Timeliness of documentation for incident reports; (2) Delegating routine tasks to junior staff earlier in the project cycle.

Development Plan 2025: Attend a one-day workshop on project management for research facilities in February. Will also take on the role of deputy safety officer for the lab, with a transition period in Q1.

Employee Signature: N. Huda (signed 20 Dec 2024)
Supervisor Signature: M. Tan (signed 20 Dec 2024)

---

2. Wei Lin – Research Associate

Self-Assessment: Wei Lin stated that she had completed the quarterly inventory checks on time and had processed over 400 sample requests during the year. She also mentioned that she had learned to operate the new automated aliquotter, which was installed in March. She rated herself as 3, noting that she felt she could improve her efficiency in data entry.

Supervisor Comments: Wei Lin is diligent and accurate in her work. The inventory records have been consistently clean, and she has not missed a single quarterly deadline. She picked up the aliquotter training quickly and has become the go-to person for that equipment. Her data entry speed is adequate but could be faster; she tends to double-check her work more than necessary, which is not a problem but occasionally slows down the sample processing queue.

Overall Rating: 3 (Meets Expectations)

Areas for Improvement: (1) Speed of data entry; (2) Taking initiative to suggest process improvements without being asked.

Development Plan 2025: Will be cross-trained on the DNA extraction workflow in Q1. Will also attend an Excel advanced course in March to improve her data management skills.

Employee Signature: W. Lin (signed 19 Dec 2024)
Supervisor Signature: M. Tan (signed 19 Dec 2024)

---

3. Daniel Tan – Laboratory Technician

Self-Assessment: Daniel reported that he had been responsible for the daily temperature monitoring of all freezers and refrigerators, and that he had logged all readings without any missed days. He also helped with the installation of the new backup generator in September. He rated himself as 3.

Supervisor Comments: Daniel has been dependable in his routine duties. The temperature logs are complete and signed off. His help with the generator installation was appreciated, though he needed a bit more supervision than expected during the electrical work. He tends to be quiet and does not always report small issues until they become larger; we have discussed this before.
